text.tspan: The Four Pillars of Computational Thinking
The thinking you do before you write a single line of code.
1. DECOMPOSITION
Break a problem too big to solve
into pieces small enough to solve.
CivicTrack: "handle a service request" becomes
take it in, route it, track it, close it.
2. PATTERN RECOGNITION
Notice what repeats, so you only
have to solve it once.
CivicTrack: a pothole, a broken light and a
water leak are all just "a report with a location".
3. ABSTRACTION
Ignore the details that do not
matter for the problem in front of you.
CivicTrack: to route a request you need its
category. You do not need the citizen's life story.
4. ALGORITHM DESIGN
Write the steps in an order that
works every time, not just this time.
CivicTrack: the exact rule that decides which
department a new request is sent to.
None of this is typing. This is the part of programming you can practise on paper, in the shower, or in a meeting.
